newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten slams China's plan to scrap HK legislature.
newsitem.headline: Patten slams China's plan to scrap HK legislature.

text.p: Governor Chris Patten on Wednesday slammed China's plan to replace Hong Kong's elected legislature upon the territory's handover to Chinese sovereignty next year and appealed to Beijing to reconsider.

"Britain has made clear repeatedly to Chinese leaders that it would be wrong and damaging to scrap this council and replace it with a non-elected body," Patten said in his fifth and final annual policy address to the Legislative Council.

"This remains our unshakeable position...I sincerely hope that even at this late stage, this bad idea can be thought about again. It is unnecessary as well as provocative and we will have nothing to do with it," he said.
Beijing, infuriated by electoral reforms spearheaded by Patten in the twilight of British rule, plans to replace the elected legislature with an interim provisional chamber.
Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30, next year under the terms of a 1984 Sino-British treaty signed without reference to the six million people of the colony.

While Patten swore to have nothing to do with the provisional legislature, he pledged to extend full assistance to his successor, the Chief Executive-designate, who is expected to be chosen by the end of this year.
